about: The kinds of held and worn looks (docs/attachment.md, Kinds; D546). Each item's data names its kind, "kind" in art/held/<item>.json or art/gear/<item>/fit.json; a skinned look with no data is a garment. mount: how it goes on (the five of docs/attachment.md). length_m: its real length along +Y, metres; size_m: its longest extent. grip_from_end_m: how far its grip is from the -Y end (the butt or pommel), metres; grip_share: the same as a share of its length. second: the extras key its off hand reaches (holding.md, section 3). classes: the move-set classes (items.ron's hold.class, holding.md section 1) an item of the kind may fight as; an item whose hold names another is of another kind. fits: how its turn is found, "detector" (a handle-axis fitter, a person checking the sheet), "person" (set once in its data by a person) or "body" (made on the base body). faces: the way an in-hand look's working end reaches further across Z, "-Z" (a one-sided head) unless given; a strung bow's limbs lean toward its string, "+Z". lead: the hand its grip rides in when its item's hold names none (holding.md's lead), "Off" for a bow, held in the off hand and drawn by the main, and for a hung look, a basket carried by its handle in the off hand (D567). The check reads this file; attach_contract.ts.

hafted.examples: an axe, a pickaxe, a hammer, a torch

shield.examples: a round shield, a heater shield

belt.examples: a quiver; later a pouch, a sheath

pack.examples: a small pack, a large pack

garment.examples: clothing, armour, a cap, a coif
